name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q19 - Glycosidic linkage positions between glucose units

questiontext.text: Three structures are given below in which two glucose units are linked. Which of these linkages between glucose units are between C1 and C4 and which linkages are between C1 and C6?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of Linkage (A)
In structure (I), the anomeric carbon C1 of the left glucose ring is connected via an oxygen bridge to carbon C4 of the right glucose ring. Thus, linkage A represents a C1—C4 glycosidic linkage.

Step 2: Identification of Linkage (B)
In structure (II), the anomeric carbon C1 of the upper glucose ring is joined via an oxygen atom to the exocyclic carbon C6 (\(\text{—CH}_2—\)) of the lower glucose ring. Thus, linkage B represents a C1—C6 glycosidic linkage.

Step 3: Identification of Linkage (C)
In structure (III), the anomeric carbon C1 of the lower glucose ring is linked via an oxygen bridge to carbon C4 of the upper glucose ring. Thus, linkage C represents a C1—C4 glycosidic linkage.

Step 4: Conclusion
Linkages A and C are between C1 and C4, while linkage B is between C1 and C6.

Final Answer: Linkages A and C are between C1 and C4, and linkage B is between C1 and C6.

answer.text: (A) is between C1 and C4, (B) and (C) are between C1 and C6
(A) and (B) are between C1 and C4, (C) is between C1 and C6
(A) and (C) are between C1 and C4, (B) is between C1 and C6
(A) and (C) are between C1 and C6, (B) is between C1 and C4

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q20 - Classification and reducing nature of sucrose

questiontext.text: Carbohydrates are classified on the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis and also as reducing or non-reducing sugar. Sucrose is a

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Hydrolysis Behavior
Sucrose has the molecular formula \(\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}\). Upon acid or enzymatic hydrolysis, one molecule of sucrose yields exactly two monosaccharide units (one D-(+)-glucose and one D-(-)-fructose). Therefore, it is classified as a disaccharide.

Step 2: Reducing Property
In sucrose, the glycosidic bond is formed between the reducing group of glucose (anomeric carbon C1) and the reducing group of fructose (anomeric carbon C2). Because both anomeric centers are tied up in the linkage, no free hemiacetal or hemiketal group is available to mutarotate or reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagents. Consequently, sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

Step 3: Conclusion
Sucrose is both a disaccharide and a non-reducing sugar.

Final Answer: disaccharide; non-reducing sugar

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q21 - Examples of globular proteins in organisms

questiontext.text: Proteins can be classified into two types on the basis of their molecular shape i.e., fibrous proteins and globular proteins. Examples of globular proteins are :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification by Molecular Shape
Globular proteins result when polypeptide chains fold tightly into compact, spherical or spheroidal shapes. They are typically soluble in aqueous solvents.

Step 2: Evaluation of Options
Insulin is a hormone composed of two polypeptide chains folded into a compact globular structure and is soluble in water. Albumin (found in egg white and blood serum) is also a classic water-soluble globular protein. On the other hand, keratin (found in hair, wool, and nails) and myosin (found in muscle fibers) consist of long, parallel polypeptide chains held together by hydrogen and disulfide bonds to form insoluble fibers, classifying them as fibrous proteins.

Step 3: Conclusion
Insulin and albumin are globular proteins.

Final Answer: Insulin; Albumin

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q22 - Branched chain polymers of glucose units

questiontext.text: Which of the following carbohydrates are branched polymer of glucose?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Features of Polysaccharides
Polysaccharides composed of glucose units can either form linear unbranched chains or branched macromolecules containing cross-linkages.

Step 2: Comparison of the Polymers
Amylose is a linear unbranched polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose linked strictly by \(\alpha\)-(1\(\rightarrow\)4) glycosidic bonds. Amylopectin is a branched polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose with \(\alpha\)-(1\(\rightarrow\)4) linear linkages and periodic \(\alpha\)-(1\(\rightarrow\)6) branch points. Cellulose is a linear unbranched structural polymer of \(\beta\)-D-glucose linked via \(\beta\)-(1\(\rightarrow\)4) glycosidic bonds. Glycogen is an extensively branched storage polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose containing \(\alpha\)-(1\(\rightarrow\)4) chains and frequent \(\alpha\)-(1\(\rightarrow\)6) branches.

Step 3: Conclusion
The branched polymers of glucose are amylopectin and glycogen.

Final Answer: Amylopectin; Glycogen

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q23 - Identification of acidic amino acid structures

questiontext.text: Amino acids are classified as acidic, basic or neutral depending upon the relative number of amino and carboxyl groups in their molecule. Which of the following are acidic?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Criteria for Acidic Amino Acids
An amino acid is acidic when the molecule contains more carboxylic acid groups (\(\text{—COOH}\)) than basic amino groups (\(\text{—NH}_2\)). When the numbers of \(\text{—COOH}\) and \(\text{—NH}_2\) groups are equal, the amino acid is neutral.

Step 2: Counting Functional Groups in the Given Formulas
\((\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{COOH}\) has one \(\text{—COOH}\) and one \(\text{—NH}_2\) group (neutral).
\(\mathrm{HOOC}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{COOH}\) has two \(\text{—COOH}\) groups and one \(\text{—NH}_2\) group, making it acidic.
\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{COOH}\) has one \(\text{—COOH}\) and one \(\text{—NH}_2\) group (neutral).
\(\mathrm{HOOC}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{COOH}\) has two \(\text{—COOH}\) groups and one \(\text{—NH}_2\) group, making it acidic.

Step 3: Conclusion
The structures with two carboxyl groups and one amino group are acidic amino acids.

Final Answer: \(\mathrm{HOOC}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{COOH}\); \(\mathrm{HOOC}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)-\mathrm{COOH}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q24 - Structural classification and properties of lysine

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification by Functional Group Position
In lysine, one of the amino groups (\(\text{—NH}_2\)) is bonded directly to the \(\alpha\)-carbon atom (the carbon adjacent to \(\text{—COOH}\)). This qualifies lysine as an \(\alpha\)-amino acid.

Step 2: Acid-Base Classification
The chemical formula reveals two basic amino groups (one \(\alpha\)-amino group and one terminal \(\epsilon\)-amino group on the aliphatic side chain) and only one carboxylic acid group (\(\text{—COOH}\)). Because the number of amino groups exceeds the number of carboxyl groups, lysine behaves as a basic amino acid.

Step 3: Essential vs Non-Essential Character
Lysine cannot be synthesized in vivo by humans and must be acquired through the diet, making it an essential amino acid rather than an amino acid synthesized in the body.

Step 4: Conclusion
Lysine is an \(\alpha\)-amino acid and a basic amino acid.

Final Answer: \(\alpha\)-Amino acid; Basic amino acid

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q25 - Monosaccharides existing in furanose ring form

questiontext.text: Which of the following monosaccharides are present as five membered cyclic structure (furanose structure)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of Furanose Ring
A furanose structure refers to a five-membered heterocyclic ring composed of four carbon atoms and one oxygen atom, named by analogy with furan.

Step 2: Analysis of Listed Monosaccharides
D-Ribose is an aldopentose (\(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5\)) that cyclizes via an intramolecular hemiacetal linkage between C1 and C4 to form a five-membered furanose ring (ribofuranose). D-Fructose is a ketohexose (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)) that forms a five-membered cyclic hemiketal between the C2 keto group and the C5 hydroxyl group, adopting a furanose ring structure (fructofuranose). In contrast, D-glucose and D-galactose are aldohexoses that preferentially form six-membered pyranose rings.

Step 3: Conclusion
Ribose and fructose exist as five-membered furanose structures.

Final Answer: Ribose; Fructose

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q26 - Intermolecular bonds stabilizing fibrous proteins

questiontext.text: In fibrous proteins, polypeptide chains are held together by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Arrangement in Fibrous Proteins
Fibrous proteins feature linear polypeptide chains arranged parallel to each other along a common axis, forming tough, thread-like fibers that are insoluble in water.

Step 2: Cross-Linking Forces
These parallel chains are locked into stable aggregates by extensive networks of intermolecular hydrogen bonds between polypeptide backbones and covalent disulfide bonds (\(\text{—S—S—}\)) formed through oxidation of adjacent cysteine residues.

Step 3: Conclusion
Disulfide linkages and hydrogen bonds are the primary interactions holding polypeptide chains together in fibrous proteins.

Final Answer: disulphide linkage; hydrogen bonds

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q27 - Identification of purine nitrogenous bases

questiontext.text: Which of the following are purine bases?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Nitrogenous Base Classification
The heterocyclic bases in nucleic acids belong to two chemical families: purines and pyrimidines.

Step 2: Comparison of Ring Systems
Purines consist of a bicyclic ring system formed by the fusion of a six-membered pyrimidine ring with a five-membered imidazole ring. Adenine and guanine are the two purine bases present in DNA and RNA. Pyrimidines consist of a single six-membered aromatic ring containing two nitrogen atoms; thymine, uracil, and cytosine are pyrimidine bases.

Step 3: Conclusion
Guanine and adenine are purine bases.

Final Answer: Guanine; Adenine

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q28 - Chemical nature and biological function of enzymes

questiontext.text: Which of the following terms are correct about enzyme?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical Composition of Enzymes
Enzymes are specialized biomolecules synthesized by living cells. Almost all enzymes are globular proteins with highly specific tertiary conformations.

Step 2: Catalytic Function
Enzymes act as biological catalysts (biocatalysts) that dramatically accelerate biochemical reaction rates by lowering the activation energy barrier without themselves being consumed in the reaction. They are neither dinucleotides nor nucleic acids.

Step 3: Conclusion
Enzymes are accurately described as proteins and biocatalysts.

Final Answer: Proteins; Biocatalysts
